drivers.claim: Demand is strong. GPU rental prices rose almost 40% from October 2025 to March 2026, capacity was booked through August–September 2026, and hyperscaler capex is about $646bn. This supports CoreWeave's roughly $102bn adjusted backlog and its $12.4–13.2bn 2026 revenue guide.

Customer concentration is a material risk. The largest customer, about 38% of revenue, used its option to cut 2027 volume by about 20%, removing about $2.1bn from backlog. Platinum ClusterMAX status supports pricing but does not eliminate the risk, especially given the 2024 price collapse when supply surged.

The balance sheet is heavily financed and the company is loss-making. More than $30bn of capital was raised this year and the Q2 net loss was $626m. Enterprise value therefore sits well above the roughly $40bn market cap. Nvidia's $6.3bn backstop partly cushions downside but is small relative to capex.

drivers.claim: Reported results and guidance imply earnings power that the roughly $5.5T market cap does not fully reflect. Data-centre revenue was $89.0B (+117%), gross margin 75%, and next-quarter revenue is guided to $108B. That is a roughly $430B annualised run rate, about 21-22x run-rate earnings on my assumed margins, with Vera Rubin ramping.

Demand signals remain strong and supply is tight. Hyperscaler capex is estimated at about $646B in 2026, H100 one-year rental prices rose almost 40% with capacity sold out, and the CoWoS gap is narrowing only slowly. Together these support continued pricing power and volume.

Risks cap the upside. Nvidia's circular financing and backstops add credit exposure, Broadcom's custom accelerators are growing fast (+221%), HBM prices are set to rise 121% in 2027, and grid delays could push data-centre capacity into 2027. Earlier rental-price declines show the cycle can turn.

parsed.rationale: At $228.38 and a market cap of about $5.5T, NVDA trades near 21-22x annualised earnings from the guided $108B quarter, assuming a net margin of about 55-60%. Upside is limited by circular financing exposure, custom-silicon competition, rising HBM costs, power delays and cyclicality. That makes the stock moderately attractive rather than a bargain. Confidence is moderate because margin and growth assumptions are my own estimates..

drivers.claim: Demand and pricing backdrop is strong. H100 one-year rental prices rose almost 40% in six months, capacity is sold out, and hyperscaler capex is estimated at about $646B in 2026. Platinum ClusterMAX status supports a pricing premium.

Contracted visibility is large relative to the roughly $40B market cap: a $104.2B backlog and 2026 revenue guidance of $12.4-13.2B. Even so, Q2 revenue of $2.575B came with a $626M net loss, so the backlog has not yet turned into profit.

Growth depends on heavy external funding (more than $30B of debt and equity raised year to date) and on Nvidia support (a $6.3B unsold-capacity backstop and about $2B of equity). This adds leverage, dilution and circularity risk that the market cap does not capture. The 2024 rental-price decline also shows how quickly pricing can turn when capacity floods in.

parsed.rationale: At $87.12 and about $40B market cap, CoreWeave trades at a modest multiple of 2026 revenue guidance and a fraction of its $104B backlog, with tight GPU supply and rising rental prices. drivers.claim: The pre-announced FQ3 FY27 data-centre revenue (>$104B, more than double year on year, gross margin >76%) implies annualised earnings of roughly $250B. That puts the $5.5T market cap at about 20-22x run-rate earnings, which looks modest for this growth.

Demand and pricing remain tight. Hyperscaler capex is about $646B in 2026, H100 one-year rental prices rose nearly 40% in six months, capacity is sold out and booked into late 2026, and CoWoS packaging is still short.

Offsetting risks: custom-accelerator competition (Broadcom guiding to $115B of AI revenue for FY27), circular financing and backstop exposure, power and grid delays, and rising HBM input costs that could pressure margins and cap the multiple.

Risks include a shift to custom ASICs, circular financing and backstop exposure, grid delays that could slip capacity, and rising HBM costs. Execution and financing risk temper the upside. Guidance needs ARR to grow 2.3-3x in H2 while only about 1 GW of 5 GW contracted power connects in 2026. Capex of $20-25B against GAAP losses implies debt or dilution, and the outcome depends on hyperscaler-driven demand persisting.

parsed.rationale: At $235.88 and about $52B market cap, Nebius trades near 6-7x guided year-end ARR. The business has 41% adjusted EBITDA margins, payback under two years on new capacity, and accelerating price increases amid a documented GPU shortage. If 1 GW connects at more than $20M per MW, the revenue capacity well exceeds what the share price implies. Heavy capex, GAAP losses, and likely dilution or debt (net debt is not given) justify a discount, as does the steep H2 ramp needed to meet guidance. Applying about 8x mid-guidance ARR, less a financing haircut, gives a fair value near $280. That makes the shares moderately attractive, with meaningful execution risk.

drivers.claim: Demand for Nvidia GPUs looks very strong. H100 one-year rental prices rose almost 40% from October 2025 to March 2026, capacity is sold out, and hyperscaler capex is estimated at about $646B in 2026. This supports high earnings but is probably already reflected in a roughly $5.5T market cap.

Competition and circular-financing risk cap the upside. Broadcom's custom-accelerator AI revenue is growing 221% year on year with a $115B fiscal 2027 AI guide, and Nvidia backstops customers such as CoreWeave, which makes part of the demand look vendor-supported.

Supply-chain and cost constraints cut both ways. CoWoS packaging gaps are narrowing, which eases supply. Power and grid delays could push data-centre deployments into 2027, and a projected 121% rise in HBM prices threatens margins.

Custom-silicon competition, vendor-financing exposure, HBM cost inflation and data-centre power delays balance the demand case. drivers.claim: Earnings power is large relative to the $5.5T market cap. Q2 FY27 data-centre revenue was $89.0B (+117% YoY) at a 75% gross margin, and next-quarter revenue is guided to $108B. That implies a run-rate of about $430B and a low-to-mid 20s P/E on run-rate earnings.

Demand and supply indicators remain tight. Hyperscaler capex is about $646B in 2026, H100 one-year rental prices rose almost 40% with capacity sold out, and the CoWoS gap is still about 10-20%. This supports further volume growth.

Risks cap the upside. Custom-accelerator competition is growing fast (Broadcom AI revenue +221%, $115B FY27 guide). Circular financing and backstops add credit exposure. Power and grid delays could push out deployments, and rising HBM prices may pressure margins.

drivers.claim: At $235.88 (about $52B market cap), NBIS trades near 6.5x the midpoint of year-end 2026 ARR guidance ($7-9B). That multiple is reasonable if guidance is met, but it leaves little margin for slippage.
